answer: Each agent can earn the right to submit claims only after locking a scarce token that is slashed if independent audits find fabricated work. Auditors are assigned by a cipher-based random draw, and a claim passes only when several auditors stake their own tokens on it. A sybil can split identities, but cannot multiply the locked value: to gain more influence, the attacker must buy and risk more tokens, while coordinating false audits exposes every stake to loss. The reef of honest agents is costly to forge because each fake identity needs real capital at risk.
